SPACE CRAFT JOURNAL / TECHNOLOGY & DESIGN TOOLS

Exploring the impact of 3D office design.

Let tools support a clearer decision. This Space Craft planning note looks at exploring the impact of 3d office design through the choices that affect everyday use, the details worth testing and the questions to take into your project brief.

Space Craft editorialPlanning note · 4 min read
IN THIS NOTEUse the visual to answer a specific questionDefine the question firstCheck the underlying informationKeep a decision recordMap activity before assigning desksBefore you decide
01 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Use the visual to answer a specific question

A 3D view can help test proportions, sightlines or a material combination. Ask which elements are accurate and which are placeholders. Check the proposal against the measured plan and the product schedule so that the image remains a useful decision aid rather than an assumed construction specification.

02 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Define the question first

A digital plan, visualisation or AI-assisted exploration should help answer a specific question about layout, scale or direction. A polished image is not evidence that the space has been resolved.

03 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Check the underlying information

Verify dimensions, product availability, services and the buildability of any visual proposal. Review automated suggestions with the appropriate design or technical specialist.

04 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Keep a decision record

Capture what has been agreed and what is still illustrative. This helps avoid treating an early visual as a final specification or a commitment about delivery.

05 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Map activity before assigning desks

Write down the tasks people perform, how often teams overlap and when visitors arrive. A desk count alone will not reveal the need for private calls, project tables or storage.

BEFORE YOU DECIDE

Take this into your brief.

  • Name the decision the tool is helping with.
  • Verify dimensions and technical assumptions.
  • Distinguish visual exploration from construction information.

Write down one priority, one constraint and one question you still need to answer. Review them beside the plan or material sample before agreeing the next design decision.

General design considerations for discussion. Product suitability, technical performance, statutory requirements and project pricing need appropriate, project-specific review. Images are illustrative.
